data.gender_notes: Naajy is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘najj’ which means to be free from sin or to be victorious. In the Quran, it is mentioned that Allah will save the believers and grant them victory. The name Naajy carries the meaning “Victorious, Triumphant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Naajy usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious, triumphant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing triumph over adversity and living a life free from sin.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naajy total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, volume 12, page 142. According to this reference, Naajy ibn 'Amr al-Misri was a tribal chief who led the Arab forces against the Byzantines at the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 AD, during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. He was killed in battle and his head was brought back to the caliph as a war trophy. Naajy is also mentioned in early Islamic poetry as a brave and valiant warrior.
historical_references.context: Battle of Mu'tah, Arab forces against Byzantines

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam's Futuh Misr, page 110. According to this reference, Naajy ibn 'Amr al-Misri was also a leader of a group of Arab tribes who settled in Egypt during the early Islamic conquest of the region. He was appointed as the military commander of Fustat, the new Islamic capital, by 'Amr ibn al-'As, the first Arab governor of Egypt. Naajy is remembered in Egyptian history for his role in repelling a major Byzantine attack on Fustat in 640 AD.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic conquest of Egypt, military commander of Fustat
